Latin word

superior

superior, superius

adjective (comparative) · Declension on Wiktionary

earlier, former (of time); last, previous, earlier; upper, higher

In this lexicon

  • former

    also used · classical · Cic. Har. Resp. 15: annō superiōre (Lewis & Short)

  • last

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. Har. Resp. 15: annō superiōre (Lewis & Short); M-O s.v. last year: superiōre annō; Traupman 89: the previous year, superior annus; Traupman 43

  • upper

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. Att. 12.10: tōta domus superior vacat (Lewis & Short); Caes. B.G. 7.46: superiōrem partem collis (Lewis & Short); Traupman 58: upper lip, labrum superius

  • superior esse: advantage

    classical

  • superior et īnferior scrīptūra: context

    classical

  • schola superior: school

    modern

  • camera superior: senate

    modern

Examples

  • quid proximā, quid superiōre nocte ēgerīs

    what you did last night, and what the night beforeCic. Cat. 1.1

    In the entry for last

  • Annō superiōre in Lūsitāniā fuimus.

    Last year we were in Portugal.composed

    In the entry for last

  • ad rīvum eundem lupus et agnus vēnerant sitī compulsī; superior stābat lupus longēque īnferior agnus

    a wolf and a lamb had come to the same stream, driven by thirst; the wolf stood higher up, and the lamb far belowPhaedr. 1.1.1–3

    In the entry for upper

    in the upper part only boating is allowed; lower down you may swim as wellPlin. Ep. 8.8.6

    In the entry for upper
